userNote: Replaced this old dual-antenna Wi-Fi router. Works electrically, just slow.

analysis.summary: A consumer 802.11n/ac wireless router with detachable RP-SMA antennas and a standard 12V DC wall adapter.

diyMethods.title: Turn into a Garage / Shed Wi-Fi Extender
steps: Hold the rear Reset button with a paperclip for 10 seconds to wipe old credentials.
Connect a laptop via Ethernet, open the admin page, and switch the mode to Access Point (AP Mode).
Disable DHCP, match your home Wi-Fi name, and plug it into any dead-zone room via cable.
diyMethods.outcome: Saves buying a new Wi-Fi extender and keeps the router in active use.

diyMethods.title: Harvest the 12V DC Power Adapter & Antennas
toolsNeeded: Scissors or electrical tape (if adapting plug)
steps: Unplug and keep the 12V DC wall brick — it powers LED strip lights, mini fans, and desktop speakers.
Unscrew the two external antennas to keep as replacements or magnetic-mount extenders for PC Wi-Fi cards.
diyMethods.outcome: Gives you a reliable 12V power supply and spare RF antennas for home projects.

safeAtHomePrep: Factory-reset the router for 15 seconds while powered on so your old Wi-Fi password is erased.
If the plastic shell is cracked beyond reuse, unscrew the casing and store the small circuit board in a dry labeled box until you have a bundle of clean PCBs.
safetyWarnings: Unplug the wall adapter completely before opening the plastic housing.
Do not burn the ABS plastic shell or PVC power cord.

userNote: Left earbud stopped playing and the Lightning cable sheath split near the plug.

analysis.itemName: Broken Wired Earphones & Frayed USB Charging Cable
analysis.summary: Tangled 3.5mm wired earbuds with damaged insulation alongside a frayed USB-A charging cable.

diyMethods.title: Rescue Micro Neodymium Magnets from Earbuds
toolsNeeded: Small flathead screwdriver or butter knife
steps: Snap open the plastic earbud shells gently along the seam using a flat tool.
Lift out the tiny circular speaker driver inside each bud.
Peel the strong mini neodymium magnet off the back of the speaker coil for fridge notes or screw trays.
diyMethods.outcome: Turns dead earbuds into super-strong miniature magnets for your desk or workshop.

diyMethods.title: Salvage Good Copper Wire & Secure Frayed Cable Ends
steps: If the USB cable still charges when held straight, reinforce the frayed neck with two snug layers of heat-shrink or tape.
If dead, snip off the damaged plug and keep the intact middle copper cable length for low-voltage 5V LED or battery craft wiring.
diyMethods.outcome: Eliminates fire risk from exposed strands while saving clean insulated copper wire.

safeAtHomePrep: Never keep using a frayed charging cord near bedding or rugs — coil and snip the broken connector off immediately so nobody plugs it in.
Keep harvested neodymium magnets away from young children and pets.
safetyWarnings: Never strip or burn PVC cable insulation with a lighter (releases toxic hydrochloric fumes).
Discard frayed charging connectors immediately so they cannot short-circuit a USB port.

userNote: Missing the D keycap and mouse scroll wheel skips.

analysis.summary: Standard desktop membrane keyboard with a missing keycap paired with an older optical mouse.

diyMethods.title: 5-Minute Keycap Swap & Mouse Wheel Fix
steps: Swap a rarely used keycap (like Scroll Lock or Pause) onto the missing D stem so the keyboard works comfortably again.
Remove the single screw under the mouse, blow out dust around the scroll wheel axle, and wipe the optical sensor lens with a dry swab.
diyMethods.outcome: Restores both peripherals to working backup duty in under 10 minutes.

diyMethods.title: Upcycle Keycaps & USB Cable for Crafts/Repairs
steps: Pop off all keycaps and wash them in warm soapy water.
Glue favorite letter keys onto small flat magnets or wooden tiles for custom fridge word magnets, luggage tags, or coaster borders.
Remove the AA battery (if wireless) and store it separately; keep the intact USB cord for 5V DIY lamps.
diyMethods.outcome: Turns ~104 plastic keycaps into playful home organizers instead of landfill plastic.

safeAtHomePrep: Always check underneath the keyboard and mouse for AA/AAA batteries before storing or repurposing.
Wipe down grime with mild soap before crafting with the keycaps.
safetyWarnings: Check for leaking alkaline batteries inside battery compartments and handle crust with gloves.
